subject: Geography
description: Major plateaus of the world by location and features

questions.stem: The 'Tibetan Plateau' — the highest and largest plateau in the world — lies chiefly in:
questions.explanation: Tibetan Plateau — also called the 'Roof of the World' — average elevation > 4,500 m; area ~2.5 million km². Mostly in China's Tibet Autonomous Region and Qinghai Province. Extends into Ladakh (India) and small parts of Bhutan and Nepal. Source of major Asian rivers — Indus, Brahmaputra, Ganges (via tributaries), Yangtze, Mekong, Yellow River.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Deccan Plateau' of peninsular India is bordered by:

options.option_text: Satpura hills on the north, Western and Eastern Ghats on the sides

questions.explanation: Deccan Plateau — roughly triangular. Northern edge — Satpura hills (with the Vindhyas just beyond, north of Narmada). Western edge — Western Ghats (rising up from the Arabian Sea coast). Eastern edge — Eastern Ghats (lower, more broken). The plateau tilts gently eastward — which is why major peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri) flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Colorado Plateau' — famous for the Grand Canyon — lies in:
questions.explanation: Colorado Plateau — in the southwestern USA, covering parts of Utah, Arizona, Colorado and New Mexico. Average elevation ~2,000 m. The Colorado River has carved the Grand Canyon (~1.6 km deep) across this plateau over 5-6 million years. Other famous US landmarks here — Monument Valley, Bryce Canyon, Zion, Mesa Verde.

questions.stem: Match the plateau with the continent where it lies. A. Ethiopian Highlands. B. Brazilian. C. Anatolian. D. Australian. List-II: 1. Africa, 2. South America, 3. Asia, 4. Oceania/Australia.
questions.explanation: Ethiopian Highlands (Africa) — source of the Blue Nile. Brazilian Plateau (S. America) — covers much of central/eastern Brazil. Anatolian Plateau (Asia) — covers most of Turkey. Australian Plateau / Western Plateau (Oceania). Other big ones — Iranian (Asia), Bolivian / Altiplano (S. America), African Plateau south of the Sahara.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Chota Nagpur plateau is a major source of minerals in India — especially:
questions.explanation: Chota Nagpur Plateau (Jharkhand, parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, WB) — India's 'mineral storehouse'. Coal (Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih); iron ore (Jharkhand/Odisha); bauxite; copper; mica. Ranchi and Jamshedpur are major industrial cities here. The Damodar river (Bengal's 'sorrow' before the Damodar Valley Corporation dams) flows through it. Petroleum is chiefly offshore (Mumbai High) and in Assam.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The 'Altiplano' — the vast, arid highland plateau in South America — is in:
questions.explanation: Altiplano — 'high plain' — lies in western Bolivia and southern Peru, in the Andes. Second-highest plateau in the world after Tibet. Contains Lake Titicaca (world's highest navigable lake, ~3,812 m) and Uyuni salt flat (world's largest salt pan, rich in lithium). Capitals La Paz (Bolivia) and Puno (Peru) sit on the Altiplano.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: A plateau formed by extensive lava flows is called a:
questions.explanation: Volcanic / lava plateaus form when lava flows from many fissures cover a large area and solidify. Example — Deccan Traps (India) — huge lava plateau laid down ~65 million years ago, some theories linking it to the K-Pg mass extinction; Columbia River Plateau (USA); Drakensberg in Ethiopia. Piedmont plateau — 'at the foot of mountains' (e.g., near the Appalachians). Intermontane — between mountains (e.g., Tibet, between Himalayas and Kunlun).
